gap: No result ChatGPT got states that DC Rainmaker measured the Garmin Instinct 3 Solar burning 0.3% of its battery per hour in GPS-only mode (a 300+ hour projection), against a 58-hour projection for the AMOLED Instinct 3 on the same ride, or that OutdoorGearLab got only 16 hours of continuous GPS from the Apple Watch Ultra 3 against 40 hours from the Amazfit T-Rex 3.
standout_why: Compared against the cited mobileplustech.com guide (published 2026-11-01, updated 2026-11-12). It lists only maker claims (10 ATM, 'longest battery estimates') with no tester numbers, no hours and no nits. Also compared against smartwatchinsight.com, the only top result that says 'Tested'. Its battery figures are spec-style (Instinct 3 Solar 'Up to 50 hours GPS', Ultra 3 '~36 hours typical'), it names no tester, and it has no Solar-vs-AMOLED comparison. The cited TechRadar T-Rex 3 Pro review and TechRadar's best Garmin watches page came back truncated, so their contents are unchecked.
decides: Confirms the Garmin Instinct 3 Solar as the rugged pick when battery matters. In DC Rainmaker's tests it ran about 2x the AMOLED version with navigation on (75 h vs 41 h) and far longer in GPS-only mode. The page also needs to say that the Solar and AMOLED versions are different buys. OutdoorGearLab's 16 h for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 against 40 h for the Amazfit T-Rex 3 limits the Ultra 3 to iPhone owners who don't need multi-day tracking. Notebookcheck's 2,650-nit reading supports the T-Rex 3 Pro as the brightest-screen value option.

findings.label: GPS-only battery drain, measured (DC Rainmaker)
findings.value: 0.3%/hour on a 3-hour road ride (projected 300+ hours) vs AMOLED Instinct 3 projected 58 hours on the same ride
findings.source_title: Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review (AMOLED & Solar), DC Rainmaker, published 2025-01-30
findings.note: GPS-only, optical HR on, no navigation. The Solar dropped from 100% to 99% about 25 minutes in and then held, so 300+ hours is a floor. Projections are extrapolated from the drain he measured on the ride.

findings.label: Battery projection, 12-hour mountain hike with navigation (DC Rainmaker)
findings.value: Solar about 75 hours vs AMOLED about 41 hours
findings.source_title: Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review (AMOLED & Solar), DC Rainmaker, published 2025-01-30
findings.note: GPS-only, navigation on, optical HR on. He also reports multiband/SatIQ at about 50-80 h (Solar, limited data because of crashes) vs about 35-45 h (AMOLED).

findings.label: Solar charge gain, measured (DC Rainmaker)
findings.value: +18 to +20 percentage points in about 3h45m (20% to 38% and 20% to 40%, 287k-328k lux-hours); Instinct 2X gained +5 points in the same window
findings.source_title: Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review (AMOLED & Solar), DC Rainmaker, published 2025-01-30
findings.note: Two 50 mm Solar units, 1:47 PM to 5:27 PM. A second, partly cloudy test of about 5h30m gave +15 and +16 points.

findings.label: Measured weight and field findings (CleverHiker)
findings.value: 51 g measured (53 g claimed); elevation gain undercounted by up to 500 ft on big-climb days; solar delayed drain 'only a few hours at most'
findings.source_title: Garmin Instinct 3 Solar GPS Watch Review, CleverHiker (Miles Knotek), updated 2026-05-18
findings.note: Distance on the control loop was off by 'only a few hundredths of a mile'. Solar charging was inconsistent under clouds or long sleeves.

findings.label: Lab test (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: About 30 hours of standard GPS, matching Garmin's claim; HR within ±3-6 BPM of a Polar H10; 1.90 oz
findings.note: 48 mm AMOLED tested, not the Solar. GPS was tested on a known 2.80-mile course. With always-on display: just under 7 days of mixed use. Overall score 78, battery 5.2/10.

findings.label: Lab test (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: 40 hours of continuous GPS; 150 min charge; HR within ±2-4 BPM of a Polar H10; 2.5 oz
findings.note: Always-on display off, no mapping, minimal interaction. Overall score 73 (ranked 13th of 13), battery 5.7/10.

findings.label: Measured brightness and battery (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 1,978 cd/m² peak (ambient light sensor on), 598 cd/m² manual max; about 12 days with always-on display; 4% per hour of high-accuracy GPS on a bike ride
findings.source_title: Amazfit T-Rex 3 review: The durable smartwatch defies the extremes, Notebookcheck (Daniel Schmidt), 2024-09-15
findings.note: The 12 days came with many notifications, all vitals on and one workout a week. The bike-ride average HR was within 2 bpm of a Polar H10.

findings.label: Smartwatch battery, real use (DC Rainmaker)
findings.source_title: Amazfit T-Rex 3 GPS Watch In-Depth Review, DC Rainmaker, 2025-01-05
findings.note: He gets about a week with frequent 2-4 hour GPS workouts. He rated GPS accuracy solid, except open-water swimming.

findings.label: Measured brightness and battery (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 2,650 nits measured at screen center (3,000 nits claimed); about 2 weeks per charge; HR 2.6% average deviation from a Polar chest strap
findings.source_title: Robust smartwatch with offline navigation: Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro review, Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten), 2026-02-21
findings.note: 48 mm, 700 mAh. The 2 weeks came with HR every 5 min, auto brightness, 8 s screen timeout and occasional non-GPS workouts. GPS was judged high-accuracy against a Garmin Venu 2. Charging: just under 50% in 30 min, full in under 90 min. RRP $399.99.

findings.label: Lab test (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.value: 16 hours of continuous GPS; 76 min charge; exactly 2.0 mi on a known 2-mile course; HR within ±1 BPM of a Polar H10; 2.2 oz
findings.source_title: Apple Watch Ultra 3 Review, OutdoorGearLab (Matthew Richardson), 2025-11-18
findings.note: Full GPS, no power saving. Overall score 85 (ranked 3rd of 13), battery 4.4/10. List price $799. On the same test, Garmin Enduro 3 measured 120 h.
